# WaveBase

> WaveBase is a schema-migration tool for Hibernate/JPA projects on the JVM (Java 17+), inspired by Entity Framework Migrations and Django's makemigrations/inspectdb. Your `@Entity` classes are the source of truth: WaveBase diffs them against a committed Model Snapshot and writes a versioned Migration with plain SQL files per dialect (PostgreSQL, MySQL, H2). It ships as a Gradle plugin and a Maven plugin with identical behaviour.

Status: pre-release (`0.1.0-SNAPSHOT`), not yet published to Maven Central or the Gradle Plugin Portal. Relational databases only.

This file is written for AI coding agents. Follow the rules below exactly; they encode decisions that are not obvious from the code.

## Core concepts

- Entity Model: the `@Entity`-annotated classes in the project's `main` source set, read by reflection after compilation.
- Model Snapshot: `src/main/resources/db/model-snapshot.json`. Committed to git. The last known state of the Entity Model. Never edit it by hand; it is rewritten by generate-migration.
- Migration: a directory `src/main/resources/db/migration/<version>/` where `<version>` is a timestamp `yyyyMMddHHmmssSSS` plus a 3-digit counter (e.g. `20261010143005123001`). Contains `postgresql.up.sql`, `mysql.up.sql`, `h2.up.sql` and, when reversible, the matching `<dialect>.down.sql`. A missing down file means the Migration is irreversible on that dialect.
- Schema History Table: `wavebase_schema_history (version, applied_at)` inside the target database, created on first use. One row per applied Migration. Reverting deletes the row.
- Reverse Scaffold: one-shot generation of entity `.java` files from an existing database. Not a sync mechanism; run it once to onboard, then review and commit.

## Supported schema changes (v1)

CreateTable, DropTable, AddColumn, DropColumn, AddForeignKey, DropForeignKey. Column renames are seen as drop + add: review generated SQL before applying, because a rename produced this way loses data.

## Gradle setup

```kotlin
// settings.gradle.kts — until WaveBase is published, consume it from a local checkout
pluginManagement {
    includeBuild("../WaveBase")
}

// build.gradle.kts
import io.github.agallina.wavebase.core.dialect.Dialect

plugins {
    java
    id("io.github.agallina.wavebase")
}

wavebase {
    jdbcUrl.set(providers.environmentVariable("WAVEBASE_JDBC_URL"))
    jdbcUsername.set(providers.environmentVariable("WAVEBASE_JDBC_USER"))
    jdbcPassword.set(providers.environmentVariable("WAVEBASE_JDBC_PASSWORD"))
    dialect.set(Dialect.POSTGRESQL)          // POSTGRESQL (default) | MYSQL | H2
    // migrationsDirectory, snapshotFile, reverseScaffoldOutputDirectory, verifyEnabled: see defaults below
}
```

The JDBC driver must be on the project's runtime classpath (e.g. `runtimeOnly("org.postgresql:postgresql:<version>")`).

## Gradle tasks (group `wavebase`)

| Task | Touches DB | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `wavebaseGenerateMigration` | no | Diff Entity Model vs Model Snapshot; write a new Migration and update the snapshot. No-op if nothing changed. |
| `wavebaseVerifyMigrations` | no | Fails if the Entity Model changed without a Migration. Wired into `check`. Disable with `-Pwavebase.verify.enabled=false`. |
| `wavebaseApply` | yes | Run `<dialect>.up.sql` of every pending Migration, in version order, recording each in the history table. |
| `wavebaseRevert [--to <version>]` | yes | Without `--to`: revert the most recent applied Migration. With `--to`: revert every applied Migration after `<version>` (exclusive), newest first. Fails on irreversible Migrations. |
| `wavebaseMarkApplied --version <v>` | yes | Record `<v>` as applied without running SQL (after a DBA ran it by hand). |
| `wavebaseMarkReverted --version <v>` | yes | Remove `<v>` from the history table without running SQL. |
| `wavebaseVerifySchema` | yes (read-only) | Compare the live database schema with the Model Snapshot; fail on any drift. Never auto-fixes. |
| `wavebaseReverseScaffold --package <pkg>` | yes (read-only) | Generate one entity class per table into `src/main/java/<pkg>`. |

## Maven setup

Until WaveBase is published, build the jars from a checkout (`./gradlew :wavebase-core:jar :wavebase-maven-plugin:jar`) and install both into the local Maven repository with `mvn install:install-file -DpomFile=<pom> -Dfile=<jar>` (add `-Dpackaging=maven-plugin` for the plugin). The POMs to use are on the site's Quickstart (Maven tab): `wavebase-core` depends on `hibernate-core 6.5.2.Final` and `jackson-databind 2.17.1`; `wavebase-maven-plugin` has packaging `maven-plugin` and depends on `wavebase-core`.

Then declare the plugin in the project's `pom.xml`:

```xml
<build>
  <plugins>
    <plugin>
      <groupId>io.github.agallina</groupId>
      <artifactId>wavebase-maven-plugin</artifactId>
      <version>0.1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
      <configuration>
        <jdbcUrl>${env.WAVEBASE_JDBC_URL}</jdbcUrl>
        <jdbcUsername>${env.WAVEBASE_JDBC_USER}</jdbcUsername>
        <jdbcPassword>${env.WAVEBASE_JDBC_PASSWORD}</jdbcPassword>
        <dialect>POSTGRESQL</dialect>   <!-- POSTGRESQL (default) | MYSQL | H2 -->
      </configuration>
      <executions>
        <execution>
          <goals><goal>verify-migrations</goal></goals>   <!-- runs during mvn verify -->
        </execution>
      </executions>
    </plugin>
  </plugins>
</build>
```

The JDBC driver must be a project dependency (scope `runtime` is enough).

Facts that matter:
- The short `wavebase:` prefix only resolves when the plugin is declared in the pom as above. Otherwise use `io.github.agallina:wavebase-maven-plugin:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT:<goal>`.
- `generate-migration` reads compiled classes: always run it as `mvn compile wavebase:generate-migration`.
- Every setting can be given in `<configuration>` (name without the `wavebase.` prefix) or as `-Dwavebase.<name>=...` on the command line.

## Maven goals (prefix `wavebase:`)

| Goal | Touches DB | Gradle equivalent |
|---|---|---|
| `generate-migration` | no | `wavebaseGenerateMigration` |
| `verify-migrations` (default phase `verify`) | no | `wavebaseVerifyMigrations` |
| `apply` | yes | `wavebaseApply` |
| `revert [-Dwavebase.to=<v>]` | yes | `wavebaseRevert [--to <v>]` |
| `mark-applied -Dwavebase.version=<v>` | yes | `wavebaseMarkApplied --version <v>` |
| `mark-reverted -Dwavebase.version=<v>` | yes | `wavebaseMarkReverted --version <v>` |
| `verify-schema` | yes (read-only) | `wavebaseVerifySchema` |
| `reverse-scaffold -Dwavebase.package=<pkg>` | yes (read-only) | `wavebaseReverseScaffold --package <pkg>` |

Behaviour is identical to the Gradle task in the same row.

Properties: `wavebase.jdbcUrl` (required for DB goals), `wavebase.jdbcUsername`, `wavebase.jdbcPassword`, `wavebase.dialect` (default `POSTGRESQL`), `wavebase.migrationsDirectory`, `wavebase.snapshotFile`, `wavebase.outputDirectory`, `wavebase.verify.enabled`.

## Defaults

- migrationsDirectory: `src/main/resources/db/migration`
- snapshotFile: `src/main/resources/db/model-snapshot.json`
- reverseScaffoldOutputDirectory: `src/main/java`
- dialect: `POSTGRESQL`
- verifyEnabled: `true`

## Rules for agents

First detect the build tool: `build.gradle(.kts)` means Gradle, `pom.xml` means Maven. Use that tool's commands throughout. Each rule names the Gradle task with the Maven goal in brackets.

1. After changing any `@Entity` class, run `./gradlew wavebaseGenerateMigration` (`mvn compile wavebase:generate-migration`) and commit the new Migration directory AND the updated `model-snapshot.json` in the same commit as the entity change.
2. Never hand-edit `model-snapshot.json` or rename/delete an existing Migration directory. If a generated Migration is wrong, fix the entities and generate again before it has been applied anywhere.
3. Read the generated `<dialect>.up.sql` and `.down.sql` before applying. Flag DropTable/DropColumn to the human: they destroy data.
4. Do not run `wavebaseApply`, `wavebaseRevert`, `wavebaseMarkApplied` or `wavebaseMarkReverted` (`wavebase:apply`, `wavebase:revert`, `wavebase:mark-applied`, `wavebase:mark-reverted`) against a shared or production database without explicit human approval. Prefer an H2 or disposable local database for verification.
5. `wavebaseVerifyMigrations` failing in `check` (`wavebase:verify-migrations` failing in `mvn verify`) means a Migration is missing: generate it, do not disable the check.
6. `wavebaseVerifySchema` (`wavebase:verify-schema`) failing means drift between the database and the snapshot. Report it; do not try to "fix" it by editing the snapshot.
7. Never put credentials in build files; read them from environment variables, or `gradle.properties` / `~/.m2/settings.xml` outside version control.
8. Reverse Scaffold is for onboarding only. After running it once, the entities are the source of truth; generate a first Migration from them.

## Typical sessions (Gradle)

Add a field:
```
# edit src/main/java/.../Post.java  (add @Column private String summary;)
./gradlew wavebaseGenerateMigration
git add src/main/java src/main/resources/db && git commit
./gradlew check
```

Manual DBA workflow:
```
./gradlew wavebaseGenerateMigration       # developer
# DBA runs db/migration/<v>/postgresql.up.sql by hand
./gradlew wavebaseMarkApplied --version <v>
./gradlew wavebaseVerifySchema            # confirm no drift
```

Onboard an existing database:
```
./gradlew wavebaseReverseScaffold --package com.acme.entity
# review, commit
./gradlew wavebaseGenerateMigration       # baseline Migration
./gradlew wavebaseMarkApplied --version <v>   # the tables already exist
```

## Typical sessions (Maven)

Add a field:
```
# edit src/main/java/.../Post.java  (add @Column private String summary;)
mvn compile wavebase:generate-migration
git add src/main/java src/main/resources/db && git commit
mvn verify
```

Manual DBA workflow:
```
mvn compile wavebase:generate-migration          # developer
# DBA runs db/migration/<v>/postgresql.up.sql by hand
mvn wavebase:mark-applied -Dwavebase.version=<v>
mvn wavebase:verify-schema                       # confirm no drift
```

Onboard an existing database:
```
mvn wavebase:reverse-scaffold -Dwavebase.package=com.acme.entity
# review, commit
mvn compile wavebase:generate-migration          # baseline Migration
mvn wavebase:mark-applied -Dwavebase.version=<v> # the tables already exist
```
